SDN Assignment 01 — Test Report

Simple Load Balancer

A POX/OpenFlow controller that transparently balances 4 clients across 4 backend servers behind one virtual service IP — tested end-to-end on Fedora 43 with Mininet.

1 · Objective

Implement a POX OpenFlow controller (SimpleLoadBalancer.py) that turns a single switch (s1) into a transparent load balancer between 4 clients (h1–h4, 10.0.0.1–10.0.0.4) and 4 backend servers (h5–h8, 10.0.0.5–10.0.0.8), fronting them with a virtual service IP (10.1.2.3).

Clients only ever see the virtual IP; the switch proxies ARP and rewrites MAC/IP addresses in both directions so redirection to a randomly-chosen backend stays invisible to both sides. Full spec: exercise1_problem.pdf. Design rationale and setup instructions: IMPL.md.

2 · Environment

Fedora 43 doesn't package Python 2.7, which POX's carp branch requires — so POX runs inside a Python 2.7 container via Podman (--network host), leaving the host's system Python untouched.

4 · Implementation summary

SimpleLoadBalancer.py implements every stub in the assignment's code skeleton. Full function-by-function rationale: IMPL.md §0.

  • State — servers_mac_to_port, client_to_port, client_to_server (sticky mapping), all keyed by IP.
  • _handle_ConnectionUp — broadcasts an ARP request for every configured server IP immediately on connect, so all 4 backends resolve before any client traffic arrives.
  • send_proxied_arp_request / send_proxied_arp_reply — build raw ARP packets via ofp_packet_out; every reply carries the load balancer's fake MAC (0A:00:00:00:00:01).
  • update_lb_mapping — picks a backend at random the first time a client is seen, then returns the same backend on every later call (sticky).
  • install_flow_rule_client_to_server / _server_to_client — one ofp_flow_mod per direction, matching only dl_type=0x0800 + nw_src/nw_dst (no microflows), idle_timeout=10.
  • _handle_PacketIn — dispatches ARP/IPv4 to the logic above; everything else is intentionally left unhandled, per spec.

5 · Test execution log

Every screenshot below is real terminal output captured while testing — nothing simulated.

STEP 1

Start POX

terminal 1
cd ~/Desktop/7sem/SDN/pox
podman run --rm -it --network host \
  -v ~/Desktop/7sem/SDN/pox:/pox:Z python:2.7 \
  bash -c 'cd /pox && python ./pox.py log.level --DEBUG SimpleLoadBalancer \
    --ip=10.1.2.3 --servers=10.0.0.5,10.0.0.6,10.0.0.7,10.0.0.8'

POX 0.2.0 (carp) starts cleanly under Python 2.7.18, loads SimpleLoadBalancer, reports LB ready. service=10.1.2.3 servers=[...], then binds and listens on 0.0.0.0:6633.✓ verified

STEP 2

Start Mininet & confirm server discovery

terminal 2
sudo mn --topo single,8 --controller remote,ip=127.0.0.1,port=6633 --mac --switch ovsk

Mininet creates 8 hosts, 1 switch, starts controller c0. The instant s1 connects, POX logs Switch connected, probing 4 servers and resolves all four: 10.0.0.5–10.0.0.8, each with MAC + port. Confirms pre-emptive ARP probing — every backend is known before a single client packet arrives.✓ verified

STEP 3

Topology / node verification

terminal 2 — mininet> (text output, no screenshot)
mininet> nodes
c0 h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 h7 h8 s1

mininet> net
h1 h1-eth0:s1-eth1    h5 h5-eth0:s1-eth5
h2 h2-eth0:s1-eth2    h6 h6-eth0:s1-eth6
h3 h3-eth0:s1-eth3    h7 h7-eth0:s1-eth7
h4 h4-eth0:s1-eth4    h8 h8-eth0:s1-eth8

mininet> h5 ifconfig
h5-eth0   inet addr:10.0.0.5  Mask:255.255.255.0
          UP RUNNING

All 10 elements up (c0, s1, h1–h8); wiring matches the intended topology one-for-one; h5's interface is UP RUNNING with the correct address and no interface errors — rules out cabling as a cause of anything seen later.✓ verified

STEP 4

Disable IPv6 noise

terminal 2
mininet> py [h.cmd('sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1') for h in net.hosts]
mininet> py [h.cmd('sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1') for h in net.hosts]

Confirmed on all 8 hosts. Purely cosmetic — quiets the Unknown Packet type: 34525 IPv6-noise lines in the POX log for the rest of testing.✓ verified

STEP 5

Baseline pingall

terminal 2
mininet> pingall

100% dropped (0/56 received) — expected, not a failure. pingall exercises every host pair; this app only ever handles traffic addressed to the virtual service IP, which isn't a real Mininet host.✓ as expected

STEP 6

Client → virtual service IP (h1–h4)

terminal 2
mininet> h1 ping -c4 10.1.2.3
mininet> h2 ping -c4 10.1.2.3
mininet> h3 ping -c4 10.1.2.3
mininet> h4 ping -c4 10.1.2.3
ClientAssigned backendPing result
h1 (10.0.0.1)10.0.0.74 sent, 3 received, 25% loss
h2 (10.0.0.2)10.0.0.64 sent, 3 received, 25% loss
h3 (10.0.0.3)10.0.0.84 sent, 3 received, 25% loss
h4 (10.0.0.4)10.0.0.64 sent, 3 received, 25% loss
SimpleLoadBalancer — per-client sequence, verbatim
client <ip> at <mac> port <n>
ARP reply: 10.1.2.3 is-at 0a:00:00:00:00:01 -> <client>
mapping: <client> -> <server>
flow c2s: <client>->10.1.2.3 ==> <server> (port <n>)
flow s2c: <server>-><client> ==> 10.1.2.3 (port <n>)
ARP reply: <client> is-at 0a:00:00:00:00:01 -> <server>

Direct, unambiguous evidence: client resolves the service IP to the fake LB MAC, controller picks a backend, installs both flow directions, and the backend later resolves the "client" to the same fake LB MAC — never the client's real MAC. Three different backends (.6, .7, .8) picked across 4 clients — real load distribution.

On the 25% loss: in all 4 cases only icmp_seq=1 was lost — the one-time cost of ARP resolution + server selection + flow install inside the controller round-trip, before a flow exists for the packet to ride on. Confirmed further in Step 8.✓ verified

STEP 7

Inspect switch state

terminal 2
mininet> sh ovs-ofctl -O OpenFlow10 dump-flows s1
mininet> sh ovs-ofctl -O OpenFlow10 dump-ports s1
mininet> sh ovs-vsctl show
ovs-vsctl show (text output, no screenshot)
Bridge "s1"
    Controller "tcp:127.0.0.1:6633"
        is_connected: true

dump-flows returned empty at this moment — over 10s had passed since the last ping in Step 6, so the idle_timeout=10 entries had already expired (expected, not a bug). dump-ports confirms the switch is healthy: all 9 ports show real RX/TX counts with drop=0, errs=0, coll=0 everywhere. ovs-vsctl show confirms is_connected: true — s1 stayed connected to POX throughout.✓ verified

STEP 8

Long stability run

terminal 2
mininet> h1 ping -c20 10.1.2.3

20 packets transmitted, 19 received, 5% packet loss, rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.038/0.080/0.406/0.079 ms. Only the first packet lost — every packet from there on succeeded with sub-millisecond RTT. Confirms the ~25% loss on short 4-packet runs is a fixed one-time setup cost, amortized down to 5% over more packets — not a recurring problem.✓ verified

STEP 9

Negative test — out-of-scope traffic

terminal 2
mininet> h1 ping -c2 10.0.0.5    # real backend IP
mininet> h1 ping -c2 10.0.0.2    # client-to-client

Both fail immediately: Destination Host Unreachable, 100% loss. Correct and expected — clients must only ever address the virtual service IP (never a backend's real IP), and client-to-client traffic is explicitly out of scope per spec. This is the app correctly not forwarding traffic it was told not to handle.✓ as expected

6 · Issues encountered & resolved

01

cd ~/pox → No such file or directory

CauseAssignment docs assume ~/pox; POX wasn't installed there.

FixCloned POX to ~/Desktop/7sem/SDN/pox instead, used that path consistently.

02

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'recoco'

CauseRunning POX carp (Python 2 code) under the host's Python 3.13.

FixRan POX inside a python:2.7 Podman container.

03

dnf install python2.7 → No match for argument

CauseFedora 43 no longer packages Python 2.7.

FixUsed Podman instead of touching host Python.

04

h1 ping 10.0.0.5 → Destination Host Unreachable

CauseInitially misread as a bug — actually the correct negative-test result (Step 9).

FixClarified: clients should never reach real backend IPs directly, by design.

05

sh ovs-ofctl dump-flows s1 printed nothing

CauseMissing -O OpenFlow10 — POX carp only speaks OpenFlow 1.0; ovs-ofctl defaults to OF1.3 and silently returns nothing.

FixAdded -O OpenFlow10 to every ovs-ofctl call.

06

POX terminal showed no new activity despite successful pings

CauseTwo POX instances running simultaneously — only one can bind port 6633; the wrong (dead) one was on screen, with ERROR:openflow.of_01:Error 98 while binding socket: Address already in use.

FixIdentified the live PID via sudo ss -lntp | grep 6633, cross-checked with podman inspect <name> --format '{{.State.Pid}}', killed the stale container.

07

Accidentally killed the working POX instance during cleanup

CauseTwo containers with similar auto-generated names — easy to target the wrong one.

FixVerified via ps -p <pid> -o pid,cmd before/after each kill; restarted clean with a single confirmed instance.

7 · Conclusion

SimpleLoadBalancer works end-to-end on Fedora 43 via a Python-2.7-in-Podman workaround for POX carp. The decisive evidence is the repeatable log sequence produced for every client:

SimpleLoadBalancer.py — per-client log
client <ip> at <mac> port <n>
mapping: <client> -> <server>
flow c2s: <client>->10.1.2.3 ==> <server> (port <n>)
flow s2c: <server>-><client> ==> 10.1.2.3 (port <n>)

combined with sustained ~95%+ ping delivery once flows are installed, correct rejection of all out-of-scope traffic, clean switch port statistics throughout, and a continuously is_connected: true controller link confirmed via ovs-vsctl show. Topology and wiring were independently verified with nodes/net/ifconfig, ruling out cabling issues as a factor in any of the above.
